exercises.name: Smith Machine Back Squat (High-Bar)
exercises.note: EXEMPLAR - already written in data-0.js, do not author

exercises.name: Smith Machine Low-Bar Squat
exercises.note: Bar 2-3 in lower on rear delts, more hip hinge and forward lean, feet set slightly further forward of the bar line than high-bar

exercises.name: Smith Machine Front Squat
exercises.note: Bar on front delts, cross-arm or fingertip rack, elbows high, feet slightly behind bar line so torso stays tall

exercises.name: Smith Machine Split Squat
exercises.note: Static split stance under the bar, both feet stay planted

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.note: Rear foot laces-down on the flat bench behind the bar line; front foot far enough forward that the knee tracks over midfoot

exercises.name: Smith Machine Reverse Lunge
exercises.note: Step back into the lunge each rep; the fixed bar path makes the balance easier than free-weight lunges

exercises.name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
exercises.note: Upper back on the flat bench set parallel to and outside the bar line, bar over hip crease, pad recommended

exercises.name: Smith Machine Glute Bridge
exercises.note: Shoulders on the floor on a mat under the bar, bar over hip crease, shorter ROM than hip thrust

exercises.name: Smith Machine Good Morning
exercises.note: Bar on upper back as in squat, hinge until torso near 45 degrees or hamstring limit, knees soft not bent

exercises.name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Start standing holding the bar, hinge to mid-shin or hamstring limit, bar stays on the thighs the whole way

exercises.name: Smith Machine Rack Pull
exercises.note: Bar starts on catches at just below knee height; heavy top-half pull, re-set on the catches every rep

exercises.name: Smith Machine Deadlift (From Low Catches)
exercises.note: Bar on the lowest catch height; fixed vertical path forces the bar against the shins, so stance is slightly behind the bar line

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.note: Flat bench centered under the bar so the bar meets mid-chest; spring hooks let you re-rack anywhere

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Press
exercises.note: Bench at 30-45 degrees, positioned so the bar touches just below the collarbones at the bottom

exercises.name: Smith Machine Decline Press
exercises.note: Bench declined 10-20 degrees, feet hooked under the bench leg roller if present; bar meets lower chest

exercises.name: Smith Machine Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.note: Hands just inside shoulder width, elbows tucked, bar meets lower chest; triceps emphasis

exercises.name: Smith Machine Seated Overhead Press
exercises.note: Bench upright at 85-90 degrees under the bar, bar starts at upper-chest catch height

exercises.name: Smith Machine Standing Overhead Press
exercises.note: Stand with head slightly behind bar line so the fixed path clears the face; bar from upper-chest catch

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bent-Over Row
exercises.note: Bar from a low catch, hinge to 30-45 degree torso, pull to lower ribs; fixed path means you set your body angle to match

exercises.name: Inverted Row (Smith Bar)
exercises.note: Bar locked on a catch at hip-to-waist height, body straight underneath, heels on floor; the lower the bar the harder

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Inverted Row (Smith Bar)
exercises.note: Feet on the flat bench so the body is horizontal; substantially harder than floor version

exercises.name: Smith Machine Shrug
exercises.note: Bar from a catch at mid-thigh, straight elevation of the shoulders, no arm bend, no rolling

exercises.name: Smith Machine Standing Calf Raise
exercises.note: Balls of feet on a plate or block under the bar for extra range, bar on upper back

exercises.name: Smith Machine Seated Calf Raise
exercises.note: Sit on the bench under the bar, bar padded across lower thighs, balls of feet on a plate; soleus emphasis with bent knee

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.note: J-hooks at armpit height, safety arms just below bottom-position bar height; free bar inside the cage

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.note: Clean grip or cross-arm rack, elbows high, bar in the front-delt shelf; safeties catch a dumped bar

exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift
exercises.note: Pulled from the floor in front of or inside the cage with safety arms swung clear; hip-width stance, hands outside knees

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.note: Wide stance, toes out 30-45 degrees, hands inside knees, vertical shin at setup, more upright torso than conventional

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Start from J-hooks at thigh height, walk back one step, hinge with soft knees to mid-shin

exercises.name: Barbell Rack Pull (From Safeties)
exercises.note: Bar rests on safety arms set just below the kneecaps; overloadable top-half deadlift, reset dead on the arms each rep

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.note: Upper back on the flat bench, bar padded over hip crease, roll the bar in over the legs; bench braced against the cage upright so it cannot slide

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.note: Bar from J-hooks at upper-chest height, press standing inside or just in front of the cage, watch the pull-up bar overhead clearance

exercises.name: Barbell Push Press
exercises.note: Shallow knee dip then drive the bar off the shoulders with the legs, press out overhead; confirm ceiling and pull-up bar clearance first

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press (In Cage)
exercises.note: Flat bench inside the cage, J-hooks at a height you can unrack without shoulder strain, safety arms just below chest level at the bottom of the rep

exercises.name: Barbell Incline Press (In Cage)
exercises.note: Bench at 30-45 degrees inside the cage, safeties just below the bottom bar path, bar touches below the collarbones

exercises.name: Barbell Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.note: Hands just inside shoulder width on the free bar, elbows tucked to 30-45 degrees, safeties set as for flat bench

exercises.name: Barbell Pin Press (From Safeties)
exercises.note: Safety arms set so the bar rests 1-3 inches above the chest; every rep starts dead from the arms, killing the stretch reflex

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.note: Torso 30-45 degrees, bar hangs at arm's length, pull to lower ribs; a touch of body english is normal at heavy loads

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
exercises.note: Torso parallel to the floor, every rep starts and ends dead on the floor, explosive pull to the lower chest, zero body english

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.note: Shoulder-width underhand grip, elbows pinned at the sides, strict curl

exercises.name: Barbell Skull Crusher
exercises.note: Lying on the flat bench, bar lowered to forehead or just behind the head, elbows fixed; spot the bar path or use modest loads

exercises.name: Anchored Sit-Up (Feet Under Foot Tube)
exercises.note: Lie on a mat with feet hooked under the foot tube / footplate at the base of the frame, knees bent 90 degrees

exercises.name: Bench Reverse Crunch
exercises.note: Lie on the flat bench, grip the bench behind the head, curl knees toward the chest and lift the hips off the pad

exercises.name: Incline Bench Cable Fly
exercises.note: Incline bench centered between the two low pulleys, D-handles, press-up then fly arc over the upper chest; remember the 2:1 ratio halves the stack number

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.note: Lat bar on the high pulley at the lat station, thighs braced under the pads or bench set under the pulley, hands 1.5x shoulder width

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Neutral Grip)
exercises.note: Both D-handles clipped to the high pulley for a shoulder-width neutral grip; elbows track straight down, bigger stretch at the top

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Underhand Grip)
exercises.note: Straight bar, palms up, hands shoulder width; biceps assist more and the elbows stay in front of the body

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.note: D-handle, half-kneeling or seated facing the mast, pull the elbow to the hip pocket, let the shoulder blade travel fully

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.note: Face the high pulley, slight hinge, arms nearly straight, sweep the bar from eye level to the thighs in an arc

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Crossover Fly
exercises.note: Both carriages at the top positions, one handle per hand, staggered stance in the center, arc hands down and together toward the belt line

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.note: EXEMPLAR - already written in data-0.js, do not author

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.note: Face away from the mast, rope behind the head, hinge slightly and extend the forearms forward-up; elbows stay by the ears

exercises.name: Rope Triceps Pushdown
exercises.note: Elbows pinned at the sides, split the rope ends apart at the bottom for full lockout

exercises.name: Bar Triceps Pushdown
exercises.note: Overhand grip on the straight bar, slightly heavier loading than rope, wrists stay neutral and locked

exercises.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
exercises.note: Kneel facing the mast, rope held at the temples, flex the spine down - ribs to pelvis - hips stay still

exercises.name: Lying Cable Pullover (Bench)
exercises.note: Flat bench a couple feet from the mast, head toward the machine, high anchor; arms sweep from overhead to over the hips with nearly straight elbows

exercises.name: Standing Cable Chest Press
exercises.note: Carriages at shoulder height, face away from the frame in a staggered stance centered between the masts, press both handles forward

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Chest Press (With Rotation)
exercises.note: One handle at shoulder height, staggered stance, press while letting the trunk rotate slightly through - core resists the twist back

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.note: Low-row position: sit on the floor mat or a low bench, feet braced on the foot tube / footplate, pull the bar to the belly with a tall chest

exercises.name: Standing Cable Row
exercises.note: Carriage at chest height, split stance, row the handles to the lower ribs; hips and shoulders stay square

exercises.name: Cable Rear-Delt Fly (Reverse Crossover)
exercises.note: Carriages at upper-chest height, grab the LEFT cable with the RIGHT hand and vice versa, pull arms apart and back with nearly straight elbows

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop (Horizontal)
exercises.note: Carriage at chest height, stand side-on, both hands on one handle, rotate the trunk to sweep the handle across the body; hips lead, arms stay long

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.note: Anti-rotation: stand side-on to the mast, handle at the sternum, press straight out and hold - the cable tries to twist you toward the machine

exercises.name: Cable External Rotation
exercises.note: Carriage at elbow height, stand side-on with the working arm AWAY from the mast, elbow pinned at the side bent 90 degrees, rotate the forearm outward

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
exercises.note: Both carriages at the bottom, staggered stance in the center, sweep the handles up and together to eye level; upper-chest emphasis

exercises.name: Cable Curl (Bar)
exercises.note: Straight bar on one low pulley, step back a foot, elbows pinned; constant tension through the whole arc

exercises.name: Rope Hammer Curl
exercises.note: Rope on the low pulley, thumbs-up grip, curl without letting the elbows drift forward; brachialis and forearm emphasis

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise
exercises.note: Face away from the mast with the cable running between the legs or beside the hip, raise the straight arm to eye level

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.note: Stand side-on, working arm on the far side so the cable crosses the body, raise to shoulder height leading with the elbow

exercises.name: Cable Upright Row
exercises.note: Straight bar on the low pulley, pull up the front of the body to sternum height, elbows lead and stay above the wrists; stop lower if the shoulders complain

exercises.name: Cable Triceps Kickback
exercises.note: No attachment needed - grip the cable end or ball stop; hinge over, upper arm parallel to the floor, extend straight back

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
exercises.note: Ankle strap (or a D-handle looped over the foot) on the low pulley, face the mast holding the upright, drive the leg straight back without arching the lower back

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.note: Face AWAY from the mast with the rope between the legs, walk out until the stack lifts, hinge and snap the hips through

exercises.name: Standing Cable Hip Abduction
exercises.note: Strap on the ankle FARTHER from the mast, cable crosses in front of the standing leg, sweep the working leg out to the side, torso tall

exercises.name: Cable Deadlift
exercises.note: One low handle in each hand standing centered between the masts, squat-hinge down and stand tall; friendly way to groove the pull with constant tension

exercises.name: Cable Standing Calf Raise
exercises.note: Handles held at the sides from the low pulleys, balls of feet on a plate; light by design - work high reps and full pauses

exercises.name: Landmine Press (Standing)
exercises.note: Bar sleeve in the landmine pivot at the base of the frame; press the loaded end from the shoulder up-and-forward in an arc, one arm at a time

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
exercises.note: Inside knee down, outside foot planted, press with the arm on the kneeling side; the position locks the ribs down and grooves a clean press line

exercises.name: Landmine Row
exercises.note: Straddle the bar facing the pivot, hook a D-handle under the sleeve (or grip the sleeve), hinge and row to the chest

exercises.name: Meadows Row
exercises.note: Stand perpendicular to the bar, outside hand takes an overhand grip on the very end of the sleeve, wide elbow flare, big upper-back stretch at the bottom

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.note: T-bar handle hooked under the sleeve, straddle the bar, 45-degree torso, drive the elbows back; strongest loading of the landmine rows

exercises.name: Landmine Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Face the pivot holding the sleeve end with both hands, hinge back - the arc gently pulls you forward so the hips must counter it

exercises.name: Landmine Squat to Press
exercises.note: Hold the sleeve end at the chest with both hands, squat, then stand and press the bar away in one flow; a garage-friendly thruster

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.note: Hold the sleeve end at arm's length at chest height, sweep the bar in a controlled arc side to side; hips pivot, arms stay long, load stays light

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.note: Overhand grip just outside shoulder width on the 28mm bar; dead hang to chin over bar; standards use ADDED weight (bodyweight counts toward the total)

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.note: Underhand shoulder-width grip, biceps assist heavily, chest to the bar at the top

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
exercises.note: Palms facing each other on the neutral handles of the multi-grip bar; usually the most shoulder-friendly pull-up

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Up
exercises.note: Dead hang, then pull the shoulder blades down and together WITHOUT bending the elbows - a few inches of rise only; the foundation of every pull-up

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.note: Loop a band over the pull-up bar (or between the band pegs), knee or foot in the loop; the band helps most at the bottom where you are weakest

exercises.name: Dip (Dip Handles)
exercises.note: Dip handles mounted on the uprights at just above standing elbow height; lean forward slightly for chest, stay vertical for triceps; standards use ADDED weight

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Dip
exercises.note: Band stretched across the dip handles, knees kneeling in the band; reduces bodyweight most at the bottom of the dip

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.note: Dead hang from the pull-up bar, pull the knees to hip height or higher, tilt the pelvis under at the top - no swinging

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.note: Straight legs raised to horizontal or above; the long lever makes this dramatically harder than the knee raise
